question: Do response-side signals (response content-type, response body digest, response timing, response status sequences) captured via Playwright route interception on locally-hosted SPAs with state-dependent server responses provide predictive PMI on within-URL transitions where client-side request signatures are identical across states?
hypothesis: Response-side signals provide predictive PMI (>=0.1 bits) on at least 2/3 of locally-hosted SPAs where request-side signatures show 0.0 bits PMI (multistep_form, wizard). Specifically: (1) Response body digests encode step-specific information (step number, step name, validation results) that request-side signatures miss; (2) Response status codes vary by step (200 vs 201 vs 400); (3) Response timing may correlate with step complexity. This tests whether server-observable communication (what comes back) provides predictive state information beyond client-observable communication (what goes out).
falsifier: Response-side PMI < 0.1 bits on >=2/3 of locally-hosted SPAs where request-side PMI was 0.0 bits (multistep_form, wizard), OR response-side PMI not statistically significant (permutation p > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction for 3 comparisons), OR positive control fails (synthetic SPA response-side PMI < 0.5 bits), OR null control fails (shuffled-label permutation p < 0.01).
baselines: Request-side PMI from parent experiment EXP-PHYSICS-34674671762 (dashboard 0.881 bits, multistep 0.0 bits, wizard 0.0 bits)
URL-only PMI (trivial zero on single-path SPAs)
Shuffle null (action labels permuted within trajectories)
positive_control: Synthetic SPA with deterministic response-side variation: 8 states, 4 actions, each (state, action) triggers distinct response body (JSON with state-specific data), status code (200-201), and content-type. Response-side PMI >= 0.5 bits with permutation p < 0.001.
null_control: Shuffled action labels on real SPA data (dashboard, multistep_form, wizard). Permutation p > 0.01 after Bonferroni correction.
measurement_validity: Same 3 locally-hosted SPAs as parent experiment (dashboard, multistep_form, wizard) to control for site properties
Response-side data captured via Playwright route interception: response.status(), response.headers(), response.body() (SHA-256 digest), response.timing()
Response state discretization: SHA-256(content-type + response_body_digest[:500] + status) per request, aggregated per transition as sorted tuple
Proper 80/20 temporal split with n_test >= 30 on held-out test set (fixes parent wizard temporal-split violation)
Null control run on real SPA shuffled labels per spec (fixes parent null-control-wrong-population finding)
Positive control uses synthetic SPA with response-side variation (not request-side variation) to validate pipeline
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) response-side PMI >= 0.1 bits on >= 2/3 of locally-hosted SPAs where request-side PMI was 0.0 bits (multistep_form, wizard), (2) permutation p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction for 3 comparisons, (3) positive control passes (synthetic response-side PMI >= 0.5 bits, p < 0.001), (4) null control passes (shuffled-label p > 0.01), (5) no pipeline errors, verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST for C-WEB-DYNAMICS. If primary condition fails OR controls fail, verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING. If sample sizes insufficient or pipeline errors, verdict = MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: Demonstrates that server-observable communication (response bodies, status codes, timing) provides predictive state information beyond client-observable communication. This informs SPIDER architecture: response-side signals should be captured and used for state representation, especially on session-tracked SPAs where client requests are invariant. Product lane should integrate response-side state representation into the observation layer.
product_consequence_negative: If response-side signals fail to provide predictive PMI, it suggests that (a) locally-hosted SPAs with session-cookie tracking do not expose state information in responses, or (b) response body digests are too coarse to capture step-specific variation, or (c) Playwright route interception does not capture response-side data with sufficient fidelity. Physics lane should then focus on other approaches (e.g., DOM-based, timing-based, or production SPAs with richer response patterns). Does NOT falsify C-WEB-DYNAMICS entirely - only this specific detection method on locally-hosted SPAs.
estimated_cost: Low: re-use existing locally-hosted SPAs, modify capture script to capture response-side data, re-run PMI computation with response-side state discretization. ~400 transitions total (synthetic 250, dashboard 160, multistep 120, wizard 32), 12 train/test splits, 12 baseline fits.
expected_information_gain: High: This is the first test of response-side signals as predictive state representation. A positive result justifies integrating response-side state into SPIDER's observation layer; a negative result constrains the server-observable hypothesis. Testing on the same 3 SPAs as parent experiment allows direct comparison of request-side vs response-side predictive power.
